subject.title: Plugin installs crash Express 4.x routes: core npm-shrinkwrap pins path-to-regexp@8.x but no central override covers plugins

question: Should managed npm plugin installs continue inheriting all host package overrides, or should OpenClaw scope or filter those overrides so third-party Express 4 dependency graphs remain plugin-owned?
rationale: The current behavior is documented and tested as a host security-pin mechanism, but it can break legitimate plugin dependency graphs; changing it is a policy boundary, not a narrow mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Design scoped override policy
options.body: Preserve security-critical host pins only where explicitly intended and add conflict detection for plugin dependency ranges before install/update proceeds.

options.title: Validator-only warning
options.body: Keep inherited overrides unchanged but detect Express 4/path-to-regexp conflicts and fail with a clear plugin-author action.

options.title: Keep plugin-owned workaround
options.body: Require affected plugin packages to publish their own compatible dependency graph or migrate to Express 5, documenting OpenClaw's inherited override behavior as intentional.

recommendation.title: Design scoped override policy
recommendation.body: Preserve security-critical host pins only where explicitly intended and add conflict detection for plugin dependency ranges before install/update proceeds.
